A hotel with a point of view. Eighty-six rooms, a neighborhood restaurant, a corner bar, and a quiet wellness floor, connected to the city, not isolated from it.

01 — The Idea

We didn't build a hotel to disappear from the city. We built one that belongs to it: a designed home, a neighborhood restaurant, a corner bar, and a few rooms worth staying in. Austin is right outside the door.

Character

Design, neighborhood culture, and a point of view over a chain.

Local

A restaurant, a bar, and a coffee counter the neighborhood actually uses.

Human

A city note with three places worth walking to, left at the door.

02 — The Entrance

A corner of West 6th, kept a little quieter.

No marble lobby, no wall of crystal. A limestone and warm-brick façade, a discreet canopy, a single brass line set into the threshold. You're met by name and led inside. The city stays close, but the noise stays at the door.

03 — The House

A lobby that behaves like a living room.

Warm plaster and oak paneling, a sculptural reception desk in stone and brass, low leather and linen furniture, oversized art, and plants used the way a careful host would use them, sparingly. Row Coffee pours at the corner of the room.

Row Coffee

Espresso, cold brew, pastries: the lobby's morning corner.

The Row Bar

Fifty-four seats, a short honest list, the room after dinner.

Business Lounge

A quiet room to work, with good coffee and fast Wi-Fi.

Room 412 · The Corner
04 — The Rooms

Your room. Your city. Your stay.

Oak floors, linen bedding, a reading chair drawn to the light. A stone side table, integrated lighting, a concealed minibar, and a welcome card written by hand. Eighty-six rooms, drawn to feel like a well-kept apartment, not a hotel room.

  • Floor-to-ceiling windows, deep reveals
  • Oversized upholstered bed, linen bedding
  • Sculptural reading chair & stone side table
  • Concealed minibar, curated art, premium stationery
  • Handwritten welcome card on cotton paper

05 — The Bath

Stone, brass, and a great deal of quiet.

Limestone walls, a sculptural stone basin, a frameless mirror that catches the morning. Brushed brass where the hand meets the metal. Amenities in cream and clay, drawn like an independent skincare house rather than a hotel giveaway.

LimestoneBrushed brassSculptural basinFrameless mirror
06 — Dining

ROW HOUSE

ROW HOUSE — Kitchen & Wine

Modern American cooking with seasonal ingredients, served in a room that feels like a neighborhood restaurant, because it is one.

Linen menus in dark covers, a short wine list kept honest, stoneware and candlelight. The kitchen sits behind a low wall. Ninety-six seats, plus an eighteen-seat private dining room for the nights that need one.

07 — Wellness

Arden Wellness, kept small and private.

Not a resort spa. A small, private wellness floor: massage and recovery, facial treatments, yoga and stretching, and a fitness studio. The rooftop terrace is for the hours that aren't sleeping. Everything the house offers is available; nothing is pushed upon you.

08 — Details

The key is brass. The note is the city.

A matte room key on a brass fob, the AR mark debossed rather than printed. An Arden City Note pressed into your hand at arrival: three places worth walking to, chosen by the concierge. Restraint is the only flourish.

09 — Amenities

A skincare house, quietly signed with an AR.

Cream packaging, clay type, the monogram debossed into the cap. Shampoo, conditioner, body wash, lotion, soap, and the small kits, drawn to read as an independent collection, not a hotel giveaway.
